chapter_title: Trial Balance and Rectification of Errors

concepts.title: Trial Balance Agreement Check
concepts.definition: A verification procedure that compares the total of all debit balances against the total of all credit balances to ensure arithmetical consistency.
concepts.key_idea: In double-entry bookkeeping, total debits must equal total credits.

solution_steps.action: Calculate the absolute difference between total debits and total credits
solution_steps.explain: The discrepancy is the positive difference between the sum of debit balances and the sum of credit balances.

concepts.title: Wrong Side Posting Detection
concepts.definition: A technique to identify if a transaction was posted to the opposite side of an account by checking if the trial balance difference is divisible by two.
concepts.key_idea: Posting an entry to the wrong side doubles the error amount, creating a trial balance difference equal to twice the transaction value.

solution_steps.action: Divide the trial balance difference by two
solution_steps.explain: Since posting to the wrong side doubles the error, dividing the total difference by two yields the original transaction amount.

concepts.title: Transposition Error Check
concepts.definition: A diagnostic check where a trial balance discrepancy divisible by nine indicates a possible transposition of digits or a misplaced decimal point.
concepts.key_idea: The mathematical difference between any number and its transposed counterpart is always divisible by nine.
question_patterns: verify if the trial balance difference of ... is a transposition error
check if the discrepancy ... could be due to transposed figures

explain transposition error check
what do you mean by transposition error check

solution_steps.action: Check if the difference is divisible by 9
solution_steps.explain: If the difference divided by 9 has a remainder of 0, it is highly likely that a transposition error occurred.

concepts.title: Rectification of Short Amount Posting
concepts.definition: Correcting an error where a transaction is posted to the correct side of an account but with a lower amount than required.
concepts.key_idea: Add the difference to the same side of the account to bring it to the correct balance.

solution_steps.action: Subtract the recorded amount from the correct amount
solution_steps.explain: The difference represents the shortfall that must be posted to the same side of the account.

concepts.title: Rectification of Excess Amount Posting
concepts.definition: Correcting an error where a transaction is posted to the correct side of an account but with a higher amount than required.
concepts.key_idea: Reverse the excess amount by posting it to the opposite side of the same account.

solution_steps.explain: The difference represents the excess that must be reversed by posting to the opposite side.

concepts.title: Rectification of Wrong Side Posting
concepts.definition: Correcting an error where an entry is posted to the wrong side of an account with the correct amount.
concepts.key_idea: To rectify a wrong side posting, double the correct amount is posted to the opposite side.

solution_steps.action: Multiply the correct transaction amount by two
solution_steps.explain: One portion cancels the wrong entry, and the other portion establishes the correct balance on the proper side.

concepts.title: Rectification of Wrong Side and Wrong Amount
concepts.definition: Correcting an error where an entry is posted to the wrong side of an account with an incorrect amount.
concepts.key_idea: The rectification amount is the sum of the wrong amount (to cancel it) and the correct amount (to record it).

solution_steps.explain: Adding both amounts cancels the incorrect entry and establishes the correct entry on the right side.

concepts.title: Suspense Account Balance Determination
concepts.definition: Determining the initial or remaining balance of the suspense account needed to temporarily balance the trial balance.
concepts.key_idea: The suspense account absorbs the difference between debits and credits until all errors are located.
